In [[logic]], '''Nicod's axiom''' (named after the [[France|French]] [[Logic|logician]] and [[Philosophy|philosopher]] [[Jean Nicod]]) is a formula that can be used as the sole [[axiom]] of a [[Completeness (logic)|semantically complete]] system of [[propositional calculus]]. The only [[Logical connective|connective]] used in the formulation of Nicod's axiom is the [[Sheffer's stroke]].


The [[axiom]] has the following form:<math>((\varphi\ |\ (\chi\ |\ \psi))\ |\ ((\tau\ |\ (\tau\ |\ \tau))\ |\ ((\theta\ |\ \chi)\ |\ ((\varphi\ |\ \theta)\ |\ (\varphi\ |\ \theta)))))</math><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://us.metamath.org/mpegif/nic-ax.html|title = Nic-ax - Metamath Proof Explorer}}</ref>


[[Jean Nicod|Nicod]] showed that the whole [[propositional logic]] of ''[[Principia Mathematica]]'' could be derived from this [[axiom]] alone by using one [[rule of inference]], called "Nicod's modus ponens":

<math>\begin{array}{l}\varphi \\ (\varphi\ |\ (\chi\ |\ \psi)) \\ \hline \psi \end{array}</math><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://us.metamath.org/mpegif/nic-mp.html|title = Nic-mp - Metamath Proof Explorer}}</ref>

In 1931, the [[Poland|Polish]] [[Logic|logician]] [[Mordechaj Wajsberg]] discovered an equally powerful and easier-to-work-with alternative:

<math>((\varphi\ |\ (\psi\ |\ \chi))\ |\ (((\tau\ |\ \chi)\ |\ ((\varphi\ |\ \tau)\ |\ (\varphi\ |\ \tau)))\ |\ (\varphi\ |\ (\varphi\ |\ \psi))))</math><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wolframscience.com/nksonline/page-1151a-text|title = Note (A) for Implications for Mathematics and Its Foundations: A New Kind of Science &#124; Online by Stephen Wolfram &#91;Page 1151&#93;}}</ref>
